title: Chapter 200: Come to My Haunted House Next Time
html:
Chen Ge had no time to linger. Captain Yan’s call and the news about the Third Sick Hall had left him uneasy.

“Boss!” He San and Gao Ru Xue squeezed through the crowd to run toward Chen Ge. “What did you do to the Haunted House’s workers?”

“I’m only a visitor. What could I possibly do to them?” Chen Ge raised an eyebrow. “And why aren’t either of you worried about my safety?”

He San and Gao Ru Xue fell silent. Ordinarily, they should have worried when a visitor was left alone in a Haunted House. Yet the moment they saw Chen Ge enter, they had become concerned for the employees instead.

“Of course, we were worried about you.” He San flashed his signature smile, not at all awkward at his lie.

“Fine. Visit my Haunted House when you have time. I’ve added new scenarios, and I promise they’ll be exciting.” Anxious to leave, Chen Ge removed the heart monitor and audio recorder from beneath his shirt, then turned to the proprietor. “My heart rate never exceeded one hundred, correct?”

“Right, the lowest was 60, and highest was just over 90.”

“Over ninety? Why so high?” Chen Ge was genuinely surprised. Tian Teng Medical School had felt as relaxing as coming home, yet his pulse had still risen considerably. Seeing his dissatisfied expression, the proprietor nearly wept as despair overwhelmed him. “Brother, this is our opening day…”

“Raising my heart rate that much is impressive. Still, compared with New Century Park’s House of Horrors—accessible by the No. 13 bus—you have room to improve,” Chen Ge declared. “Your attraction is strong enough that you don’t need underhanded tactics, such as attacking a local competitor or exploiting a real tragedy for publicity.”

Looking over the traumatized actors, Chen Ge’s mind began to work. “Your set design is professional, and the backstory is compelling. You even weave puzzle-solving through two separate narratives. Honestly, I enjoyed myself.”

Fun? You had fun inside the Haunted House?

Despite the praise, the proprietor and actors felt little joy. “We lost. We’ll remove the unfair claims we made about your Haunted House online.”

“Thank you. If you encounter similar trouble again, feel free to contact me. Your professionalism impressed me.” The “pregnant ghost’s” expression and the “corpse’s” stare had clearly been perfected through countless hours before a mirror. Tian Teng Medical School’s experienced actors were its greatest asset.

“That’s all. Get back to work, and remember to visit me when you’re free.” Chen Ge looked over the proprietor and actors, smiled, and turned away without gloating or sarcasm.

The staff had abandoned him inside while they evacuated—an accident by any reasonable definition. A private incident might have been concealed, but this had occurred before a crowd. If Chen Ge chose to make an issue of it, Tian Teng Medical School could be finished. Instead, he praised the attraction, surprising the proprietor and leaving him grateful.

The guy is not as bad as I thought. Perhaps like us, he is not in it for the money but the meaning of true terror.

Watching Chen Ge leave, the proprietor remembered his younger self, who had adored ghost stories and practical jokes. The difficult economy made me obsess over profit. I forgot why I opened a Haunted House in the first place.

The proprietor was far too trusting. Chen Ge had never regarded them as serious competition. His gracious speech merely laid the groundwork for absorbing Tian Teng Medical School into his future horror-themed amusement park.

“Boss.” The security guard tapped the proprietor on his shoulder.

“I’m fine, let’s be ready to get back to work!”

“Um…” The guard lowered his voice. “I think he took our tape recorder.”

“What? When did that happen?”

…

Only after leaving the building and boarding the bus did Chen Ge realize he still carried the recorder. I was so focused on that speech that I forgot I was holding it. I’ll return it when they visit my Haunted House.

Back at New Century Park, visitors surged forward the moment he removed the temporary-closure sign. In only a few weeks, both the Haunted House’s reputation and attendance had risen dramatically.

“We’ll open this afternoon. Don’t worry—we’ve created a terrifying new scenario that will give you the fright of your lives!” Chen Ge called Xu Wan, then entered the Haunted House and began considering how to adapt Tian Teng Medical School’s techniques.

“The update rate for my Haunted House is very fast, and it is still growing. When the hidden missions for the Third Sick Hall are completed, I’ll need to rearrange the scary scenes to add some scary items and mix in the real ghosts with fake ghosts. That will be more interesting.”

The visit had provided abundant inspiration, and he recorded every idea in a notebook before he could forget it.

At noon, Chen Ge studied the police files until he had memorized every escaped patient’s details; any fact might prove useful. After a simple lunch, he opened for business. He would not admit the public to the Third Sick Hall until its hidden missions were complete, but that posed little problem—most visitors had yet to conquer the existing scenarios.

He remained busy until 6:00 p.m. After the last visitors departed, Uncle Xu offered him a rare smile from the ticket booth. The Haunted House was lifting attendance throughout the park, and management now did everything possible to support it.

“Nice work today.”

Once Uncle Xu and Xu Wan had gone, Chen Ge returned to the staff break room. He packed the tape and red-cloth-wrapped cleaver, then searched for the white cat.

After searching the entire attraction, he found it at the top of the tree by the entrance. The clever animal seemed to sense impending trouble and had climbed beyond his reach. No amount of coaxing persuaded it to descend.

“What are you so afraid of? The place I’m going is safer than the Third Sick Hall! Come down!”
